questions.prompt: A resistor of 20 Ω has 0.3 A through it. What is the voltage across it?
Explain why the current in a series circuit is the same at every point.
questions.modelAnswer: Charge is not created or destroyed in a circuit. In a series circuit there is only one path, so the same amount of charge must pass every point each second. The current (rate of flow of charge) is therefore the same everywhere; it is energy, not charge, that is transferred to the components.
rubric: Energy transferred, not charge used up
